messages:
maria: ran a profiling sweep last night, KV cache memory creep on long contexts. main oddity: lots of tiny microblocks plus a few large slabs causing free-list skew and fragmentation. sample trace attached (see below).

jonathan: saw similar in staging at ~2k concurrent long sessions — p95 mem +18% after ~30m.

lee: what are our block size buckets currently? any non-power-of-two tunings?

maria: current allocator history: weird geometric sizes (64,192,640,1920) — legacy tuning. profiler shows small-chunk churn where small allocations can’t reuse due to alignment and size mismatch.

olivia: that explains holes. eviction churn is high because we evict small pages to satisfy large requests, leaving small holes.

jonathan: concrete numbers from a heap snapshot (trimmed):
```
free: 64x1200, 256x300, 1kx80, 4kx3
alloc: 64x1800,256x500,1kx150,4kx40
holes: 4k_holes=23, avg_hole_size=2048
```

maria: proposal idea A — compact-on-threshold: trigger local compaction when hole_ratio > 0.15 OR small_block_reuse < 0.4. lightweight, sample-driven.

lee: proposal B — rebin to powers-of-two block sizes [64,256,1024,4096] so coalescing and buddy-like behavior are simpler. fewer fragmentation modes.

olivia: another approach: opportunistic rebalancer on eviction: when freeing many small blocks, attempt to defragment contiguous runs into new consolidated slabs and free the old one. cheaper if done incrementally.

maria: rough pseudo for sample-driven compact trigger:
```
if (hole_ratio > 0.12 && background_compact_enabled) {
  for slab in slabs:
    s = sample_pages(slab, n=32)
    if (avg_fragmentation(s) > 0.3) schedule_local_compact(slab)
}
```

jonathan: main perf concern — compaction is CPU and can spike tail latency. need strict rate limits and backpressure so we don’t compact during hot p95 windows.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued: kv-cache-compact-v1 -> canary on group kv-canary-3.

lee: experiment matrix suggestion:
- A: enable background compaction on 20% of nodes (compact_threshold=0.12, sample_size=32)
- B: switch block_sizes to powers-of-two on 20% of nodes
- C: increase per-session reserve pool for long-context sessions on 20% of nodes

maria: metrics to watch during runs: p50/p95/p99 latency, evictions/sec, hole_ratio, mem_per_longctx, reclaimed_bytes/sec, cpu_compact_pct. Also watch allocator pause time.

olivia: config snippet for quick A/B rollout:
```
kv_cache {
  block_sizes = [64,256,1024,4096]
  background_compact = true
  compact_sample_size = 32
  compact_threshold = 0.12
}
```

jonathan: agree to run A and B. rollback condition: latency regressions >5% or evictions/sec increase >20%.

lee: add telemetry event 'kv_compact.run' with fields: duration_ms, reclaimed_bytes, slab_id, cpu_pct. will help tune heuristics.

maria: I'll kick off the experiment tomorrow 09:00 PST and post the initial traces here. adding heap traces and kv-alloc histograms.

olivia: please add me to the run @maria so I can monitor dashboards.

maria: @olivia added. will post results and raw logs here :rocket:

jonathan: minor note — longctx memory growth could also be from pinning elsewhere. when you post traces check for reference chains to TPU-related buffers.

maria: good call, will include full heap stacks and a filter for longctx pins.

infra-bot: canary started on node group kv-canary-3.

lee: thanks team. feels like a pragmatic plan: sample-driven compaction + block-size simplification. :thumbsup:
